angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 521,775 km at 75.66 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.2175 +/- 0.0172 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 75.66 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.75 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract): 521,775 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.84 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5245 +/- 34 K from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-184 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-184.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.612, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
